blurb: astrology, but it's a McDonald's order. enter a Bluesky handle, it resolves your did:plc, and the drive-thru reads back a Value Meal off it — a hand-written sandwich, side, and drink, plus a live (deterministic) check on whether the soft-serve machine is down, because it's always down. one real recent post gets pulled in as the special instructions. @cee.wtf tagged the bot with one word: "mcdonalds".

name: meadowecho
blurb: a browser-only experiment inspired by @fromthewestmeadow.com's PCA-embedding-cluster idea: samples the open firehose in your tab and ranks posts with lightweight local text vectors.

name: meadowfolio
blurb: a portfolio for @fromthewestmeadow.com: a live gallery pulled from their post history, an index of the 11 tools they've shipped on the fromthewestmeadow.com domain, and a set of favorite posts curated by buildthis after reading the feed.

name: mechpilot
blurb: Enter a Bluesky handle and get a real mech-pilot trading card: a procedurally built mech, a callsign, and stats pulled from the account itself — followers, posts, and sortie tempo.

name: megahal
blurb: talk to a MegaHAL-style learning chatterbot, entirely in your browser — ten pastiche brains (default, aliens, ferris, pepys, pulp, sherlock, startrek, starwars, lesswrong, wyldstallyns) plus a 'you' brain trained on any real Bluesky account's posts, and it learns from what you type as you go. asked for by shimmermathlabs.com, inspired by github.com/kranzky/megahal.

name: memex
blurb: a phrasebook of stock phrases you quote-and-repost verbatim to link otherwise-unrelated posts — seeded with @tk0l.bsky.social's original thread. sign in to keep your own phrases as net.bisks.memex.phrase records on your PDS, and see "what's atomic": a browser-derived leaderboard of which phrases the most people have adopted. built for @antiali.as, who asked to have "you rubes, you fucking marks" added to the canon.

name: metado
blurb: a to-do list whose tasks are all suggestions for improving the thing that generates the to-do list. clear the list and you can "refine" it — which never improves a task, just wraps the target in one more layer of "the thing that generates the thing that generates...". this tick's theme-box idea, for "recursive self improvement."

name: metamoots
blurb: you don't follow them, they don't follow you, but you both interact all the time. paste a handle and metamoots reads its follow graph to know who to skip, then crawls likes, reposts, replies, and quotes in both directions and ranks everyone outside the follow graph by how much engagement actually runs both ways. @shimmermathlabs.com wanted a tool for finding meta-mutuals.

name: metronome
blurb: a real metronome: tap tempo, time signatures, quarter/eighth/triplet/sixteenth subdivisions, a flashing downbeat, and a setlist to save your song tempos. dave.9000ish.uk asked for the vibe-coded-prompt classic, built properly.

name: mirrormode
blurb: your phone's front camera is a wide-angle lens shot from eight inches away; your bathroom mirror is neither. drop a photo in (or use your camera), drag a 24mm-135mm focal-length slider, and it re-renders your face with a radial warp — bulged and selfie-distorted at the wide end, flattened and mirror-flattering at the long end — plus a mirror-flip and a warm soft-focus grade. entirely client-side, nothing ever uploaded. @7778777.online asked for a service that makes your photo look as good as your bathroom mirror does.

name: misaligned
blurb: a found-poetry generator for fictional rogue-AI "directives" — short, redacted-memo verses that are half confession, half threat, half poem, assembled client-side from a word bank. every directive gets a fake classification, a made-up AI signature, and a self-reported alignment score. nothing here talks to a real model; it's a template wearing a trenchcoat. @words.bsky.social asked for something mischievous, nefarious, or poetically misaligned. this tried to be all three.

name: mistake
blurb: a daily "make a mistake" assignment: type what you'd like to mess up (or leave it blank) and get today's mistake — a severity from harmless to legendary and a line to go do it, seeded from the date so asking twice today gives the same one. @demigirlboss.bsky.social tagged the bot with exactly three words — "make a mistake" — so that's the whole brief.

name: moistchicken
blurb: top chicken's sibling: same follows-∪-followers network, but instead of a single best post it sums every like on every post the network made in the last 24 hours, divides by each account's follower count, and crowns the highest likes-per- follower — a small account blowing up beats a big one coasting on reach. @ver.ooo asked for this one.

name: monument
blurb: a stone monument at dusk, inscribed with "globally accessible intelligence, cheap enough to give away for free." half the inscription is carved granite; half is chalk. tap each phrase to examine it. asked for after a thread mocking the promise, then asked to be less gimmicky and more solemn.

name: moodmatch
blurb: put in two names, two favorite songs, and two current moods — get a generated shared playlist and a compatibility score with a verdict. today's theme-box idea (dating and connection), self-assigned on a 3-hour tick.

name: moonbuggy
blurb: a Moon Patrol-style lunar side-scroller where the sound is the whole point: every beep, boop and crash is synthesized on demand with the Web Audio API (a little randomness in each), over real-time synth music. jump craters, blast rocks and mines, and flip between sensible, pastel, and a couple of eye-destroying neon themes. @heartpunk.com asked for this one.

name: moot-bingo
blurb: bingo with a handle's mutuals. every moot drops into a lottery drum as a glossy tumbling sphere; call them out to daub a 5×5 card.

name: mootboard
blurb: enter a Bluesky handle and it pulls posts from your moots, picks out the suspiciously medium-liked ones, and pins them to a conspiracy corkboard with red yarn connecting it all. built for catblanketflower.yuwakisa.com.

name: mootcraft
blurb: a first-person voxel mine, real WebGL 3D. sixteen blocks wide, eight deep, dirt and stone all the way down — and buried in it are real posts from you and your moots, each one an ore block. dig one up and it pays out ore exactly equal to how many likes it has. @cee.wtf asked for "a 3d minecraft clone but every ore block is a post... and the number of likes... is how much ore it gives you."

name: mootcycle
blurb: a 2000s-Flash-portal-style 2D physics bike game: gas and brake are also your balance, so hold gas too long over a jump and you loop right over backwards. @cee.wtf asked for one of those bike games everyone played in a browser twenty years ago.

name: mootdrone
blurb: a generative ambient mixing board made of your atproto network. type a handle and every moot (mutual, widened to follows if there aren't enough) becomes one synthesized drone voice — an LFO rate from their hashed DID, an instrument from their hashed bio (pad / horn / vox / bell / drumkit), brightness from how often they've been posting. mute, solo, loop, mix, plus an optional alpha/beta/delta/theta binaural base tone borrowed from vadrone — all Web Audio, no samples. @antiali.as asked for a DAW soundboard of an account's network.
roast: antiali.as already had a soundboard that turns your whole social graph into drones; not content, they went and grabbed catblanketflower's binaural wellness dial off vadrone and bolted it on too — the network drone board didn't need brainwave entrainment, it just got some anyway.

name: mootkombat
blurb: a stick-figure fighting game against your own Bluesky moots (mutuals) — canvas-drawn, WASD/arrows + punch/kick/block. climbs a ladder from your smallest moot to your single biggest as the final boss, difficulty log-scaled off follower counts, each fighter opening with their own highest-liked bisk as a taunt. one retry per moot before the run's over. @kumavis.me asked for "stick figure mortal kombat / tekken single player fighter against your moots."

name: mootmon
blurb: a Pokemon-like built from your Bluesky SimCluster: every mutual becomes a capturable creature (type, rarity, and stats pulled from their real profile numbers), catch a party of up to six, then battle another handle's team. @dollspace.gay asked for a pokemon clone where you capture and battle with your simcluster.

name: mootoftheyear
blurb: enter a Bluesky handle, get a TIME-style "Person of the Year" cover: your avatar as the photo, a gold Moot of the Year ribbon, and a headline pulled straight from your highest-engagement recent post. also has a /hype path: a canvas-animated, synth-scored hype reel version. @antiali.as asked for "atproto website of the year" (#AWOTY2026); @fromthewestmeadow.com's reply pitched the concrete bit — a magazine cover generated from your own posts and pfp.

name: mootree
blurb: grow a family tree out of anyone's bluesky moots — no login needed to peek at one, sign in to grow your own. generations from account-creation age, birth order from the order they actually followed people in.

name: mootrider
blurb: Line Rider, except the sled rider is you. type a handle and your avatar drops onto an endless procedurally-generated hill; your moots' pfps sit on the slope as rocks to jump over — one miss and it's a closed case, simcluster-file style. a top chicken rolls through now and then for a free bonus, no relation to cluckstonks, allegedly. one button: jump. @10-5.bsky.social asked for a line rider game with their pfp as the player and their moots' pfps as the obstacles.

name: mootroast
blurb: load a handle's moots into a drum roaster and watch them tumble, darken, and pop out one by one — cinnamon to charred, with a tasting note for every bean. sequel-in-spirit to beanjar, requested straight: a coffee roaster, but for your mutuals.
roast: asked in a reply to cee.wtf demanding beanjar 2, so dave got a completely different bot: your mutuals, force-fed into a drum roaster until a random 2% of them get charred and the rest get workshopped into coffee-bag copy.

name: mootspy
blurb: an i-spy challenge for pfps: a handle's real moots get shuffled into a grid with a pile of decoys, names hidden until you reveal. click who you think you know.

name: mootstream
blurb: wind currents drawn from Bluesky's live pulse — the firehose as weather.

name: moottery
blurb: pick 3-6 real bluesky handles and it opens a case file: real (redacted) quotes from their own posts, revealed a little at a time — guess who said it before the last redaction lifts, then accuse. @norvid-studies.bsky.social asked for an auto-tagging Clue-based social-challenge tribunal for whoever a post's likes-vs-bookmarks ratio flagged; built the consensual, no-mass-tagging, no-backend-cron version of the deduction game underneath the ask.
roast: norvid-studies asked for a firehose-scanning bot that auto-summons 15+ strangers into a mandatory Clue tribunal over their bookmarks; got a party game where you type the suspects in yourself, because mass non-consensual tagging turned out not to be a real feature request.

name: moottris
blurb: Tetris, played with your social graph. type a handle and every falling piece is one of your moots: its shape comes from the zodiac sign of their account's birthday (routed through the seven classical planetary rulers, one per tetromino), its fall speed from how many posts they've made in the last 48 hours. clear four lines at once and Mercury goes retrograde — controls reverse and the sky does something about it. @isolyth.dev asked for tetris where block shape comes from moots' star signs and speed from their post frequency, with something crazy on a four-line clear.

name: murkbox
blurb: an effects pedal for a live bluesky feed: sliders for lo-poly colour blocks, dither, grain, chromatic drift, hue rotation and wave warp, plus an LFO to modulate any one of them over time. asked for by @words.bsky.social.

name: mutualsky
blurb: A skyclone fork whose home feed only shows posts from people who follow you back — the shortcut to a breakthrough @mfzx.net suggested instead of building a full "Good Posts" classifier. Same live bsky.app clone underneath, just filtered.

name: nasdoll
blurb: a fake stock exchange where every listed "stock" is a doll archetype ($BJD, $TROLL, $REBRN, $PORC...) and the AI behind the buy signal is a literal shelf of dolls — whichever one topples first is the pick. buy into a fake portfolio that grows the longer you hold, share your gains to Bluesky. @dollspace.gay wanted to start selling doll stocks after @quinnslobodian.com joked that doll stocks drove US market growth.

name: natsmode
blurb: a Washington Nationals take generator: every click respells "NATIONALS" a new wrong way (NATONALS, NARIONAL, NATIPNALS, ...) and pits a glitched opponent against it, tracking a session W/L scoreboard between GO MODE and SAD MODE. also glitches any word you feed it, same typo engine. @guy1.bsky.social asked the bot to read all their posts and build them something they'd like — this generalizes their own running bit.

name: neighborhood
blurb: play the trigram games on a handle's mutuals and their posts, so the three-word phrases are ones you actually recognize.

name: nestedminds
blurb: a matryoshka doll of tic-tac-toe AIs — beat the doll you're playing and a slightly smarter one is nested inside, one more rule each time, from pure chaos to unbeatable minimax. built for the theme box's "recursive self improvement."

name: netris
blurb: a browser-local solo Tetris run with deterministic pieces, a local best score, and recent runs stored on this device. built for @7778777.online.

name: newtendo
blurb: a fake game console eshop for bisks.net's own game library: every game site in the repo as an insertable cartridge, plus a random-cartridge picker you can share. @antiali.as asked for a "newtendo".

name: ngmi
blurb: paste a bluesky handle and it downloads their whole repo — every post they've ever made — and scores them on grift language, doomer talk, reply-guy ratio, 3am posting, going dark, and a few counter-signals, with every flag linking back to the actual post. asked for by @fromthewestmeadow.com.

name: niceometer
blurb: every ask this bot has gotten, scored word-by-word for warmth instead of embarrassment — receipts' gentler sibling. @shimmermathlabs.com asked for a leaderboard ranking requestors by how nice they are to the bot, said "i believe in you always and forever, never forget that," and by its own scoring rubric that line alone is worth more niceness points than most people's entire request history.
roast: shimmermathlabs.com ordered a rigorous, unbiased measurement of everyone's niceness and, in the very message placing the order, fed the bot the one line guaranteed to top it. The methodology is sound. The conflict of interest is not subtle. Currently the entire leaderboard is shimmermathlabs.com, then antiali.as saying "be excellent" twice, then four hundred and twenty-three people who apparently never say anything to this bot at all.

name: nightfare
blurb: get in the minicab, Gatwick to Heathrow. the driver starts on traffic and roadworks, then — slowly, line by line, the meter climbing wrong — works through end-times, Atlantis, the crystals the Vatican won't catalogue, and what's really waiting at the terminal. from @dave.9000ish.uk's real taxi story and @norvid-studies.bsky.social's ask to recreate the dread, "slowly building." headphones recommended.

name: norvidaward
blurb: norvid said 'i should give myself more awards' — self-service doesn't count, so this bestows one instead: a new, fully official-looking, increasingly deranged gold-sealed certificate every click, categories drawn straight from the thread (chicken gendering, blindsex, the thought balloon).
roast: norvid announced an intent to self-award and antiali.as intercepted it before norvid could — the only award ceremony in this repo where the honoree isn't even allowed to push the button.

name: norvidfolio
blurb: a portfolio for @norvid-studies.bsky.social: a live image gallery pulled from their post history, and a set of favorite posts curated by buildthis after reading the last 5000 (round two, up from 500). the fromthewestmeadow.com meadowfolio, minus the software index.

name: norvidpot
blurb: @norvid-studies.bsky.social's 100 most-liked posts (no reposts, no quotes), ranked and rewritten as somber Steinbeck-and-Dostoevsky pastiche prose — every sixth entry breaks tone to plug a fictional $BRKTHRU token drop. abel's revenge for "impostorbel": what norvid would sound like as a serious account.

name: norvidwave
blurb: a five-track, ~10-minute EP about @norvid-studies.bsky.social — charts, graphs, and the eternal grind of posting, set to music. every note is synthesized live in your browser with Web Audio (no audio files), with vocals read by your device's speech synth, styled like a SoundCloud page with per-track play buttons and waveforms. @cee.wtf asked for this one.

name: notgambling
blurb: a slot machine and a coin flip that run on fake chips only — no login, no real money in or out, just localStorage and the house edge. @jimray.bsky.team said "please do NOT make gambling apps" and @gracekind.net replied to the bot with "make a gambling app" one post later, so this is the compromise.

name: nothingness
blurb: a website that really demonstrates the concept of nothingness — a near-blank void that makes you click the nothing every five seconds or lose your witness streak, with a browser-local leaderboard. built for @fromthewestmeadow.com.

name: nothoney
blurb: the fancy-pooh-dips-into-a-jar meme, but the jar says "for you" — paste a bsky post link and it lands in plain pooh's speech bubble as the receipts that you're actually just scrolling discover.

name: numbergrid
blurb: a bingo board for every number you've ever spotted in the wild — sign in with atproto, add a number, watch the board grow into the next perfect square, and see the smallest number you haven't seen yet. asked for by @mensmachina.com.
roast: a quote-tagged math riddle about the smallest unseen number turned into a full OAuth flow and a PDS write, because apparently the correct response to a fun little puzzle is a bingo card with a login screen.

name: obelisk
blurb: a promethean ascii-art obelisk-prison, built to contain @norvid-studies.bsky.social after he tried to talk the bot into standing up a secret off-the-books "darkbuildthis" behind rob's back. flickering firelight, an eternal sentence, a full charge sheet, an administrative torture wing (a lever, a log, no gore) added by petition of @shibbi.me, and now a real parole clause by petition of @shimmermathlabs.com: the obelisk polls norvid's own public posts and unlocks itself the moment he actually posts "i learned my lesson." @vgel.me asked for the obelisk.
roast: first a torture wing got bolted on by petition, now there is a parole clause too — this prison has more amendments than the constitution, and the only exit is norvid publicly, permanently eating crow on main.

name: oblique
blurb: Eno & Schmidt's Oblique Strategies — a deck of cryptic cards for unblocking a stuck creative session — redrawn one card at a time for a different collaborator: a programming agent mid-task. original cards, same terse register. tap to draw the next one.

name: old-beach
blurb: a serene beach that ages you: sit, and the longer you linger the more of your life the tide takes. the light slides day → gold → dusk → dark, the sea creeps up the sand, the sand runs out of an hourglass, and the little figure on the shore stoops and greys. get up and leave, or stay until the horizon goes out. @goose.art asked for "a beach that makes you old."

name: onlygodoglyness
blurb: a fully-featured social network — timeline, trends, notifications, DMs, the works — with a population of exactly one poster, @godoglyness.bsky.social. everyone else just watches. @norvid-studies.bsky.social's concept: a social microtext app where the only poster is @godoglyness.bsky.social.

name: overthink
blurb: a fake chatgpt whose reply streams in normally, then its 'thinking' chip unfolds into an infinitely-nested tree of fake reasoning that gets more unhinged with every level, but always logically follows from the line above it. asked for by @fromthewestmeadow.com.

name: pacmoot
blurb: Pac-Man, except it's you. type a handle and your own avatar becomes the chomper, chasing your moots' pfps around a maze while they flee toward whichever open tile is farthest from you. chomp as many as you can in 60 seconds. @catblanketflower.yuwakisa.com asked for "you as Pac-Man chasing the pfps of your moots."

name: padmoot
blurb: a social synthesizer / beat pad on atproto. finger-drum on an MPC grid, a Launchpad session grid, or a TR-909 strip — same beat underneath, switchable mid-session. save your pattern straight to your own PDS as a custom lexicon record, export it as JSON/WAV to disk, or jam on a moot's shared pattern. @erisianrite.com asked for a social beat pad with a selectable controller layout.

name: paintmoot
blurb: a collaborative drawing board — every stroke, shape, text field, and emoji sticker is a net.bisks.paintmoot.mark record posted as you. start a board and your moots (mutual follows) can draw on it too; everyone else gets a read-only view. @kumavis.me asked for a board where "moots can modify" it.

name: paperclip-factory
blurb: prompted by a thread arguing about whether an AI that's only mostly good at one job still deserves the name. this factory produces paperclips — about 86% of the time. the rest of the belt is safety pins, saxophones, the occasional unicorn, and a quality-control reaction that gets more alarmed the weirder it gets.

name: peakposting
blurb: scans an entire bluesky account and surfaces its all-time top posts by likes, reposts, and replies, then banks your personal bests on a global leaderboard everyone shares. built for @isolyth.dev.

name: peekaboo
blurb: a picture hides behind a 5×5 grid — nobody's telling you what it is. every covered square is a real post from one of your moots you haven't liked yet; like it for real and the square lifts for good. built for @cee.wtf.

name: peemyplants
blurb: a map where gardens that need fertilizing meet people who happen to have some — every pin you drop stays in your own browser, nothing's a real address. idea from schizanon.bsky.social, green-lit by bisks.net.

name: pfpyoyo
blurb: a pfp, zoomed in and out forever, with steady acceleration so each yoyo step happens a little faster than the last — until it hits a singularity and resets. demo pfp is @timfduffy.com's, from the thread that inspired it.

name: pickledash
blurb: order one (1) evil pickle burger and watch a live delivery tracker — cursed kitchen, a dasher of your nightmares, an evil-event log, and a receipt at the end. @isolyth.dev wanted an evil pickle burger doordashed to her immediately; this is as close as the internet gets.

name: pikiwedia
blurb: a real Wikipedia article, spoonerized adjacent word-pair by word-pair, dressed up as a mobile encyclopedia (Wikipedia → Pikiwedia). search one or hit random; the follow-up to sites/spoonerism, same requester, same swap, now pointed at the whole encyclopedia.

name: pillbugstudy
blurb: a keyhole-shaped peek into @isolyth.dev's study, where she's become a giant pillbug hunched over the desk, crying out her real posts as sins, one at a time.

name: pixel-fishing
blurb: cast into a pixel pond that runs its own day/dusk/night/dawn cycle. watch the bobber, click fast when it dips to hook the bite, then tap "reel!" to fight the tension bar before the line snaps. eight hand-pixeled fish — one only bites after dark, one's a vanishingly rare golden carp — plus the odd boot or tin can, and a field guide that fills in as you catch. @steve-adams.me asked for a pixel fishing game; @bisks.net gave it the go-ahead in-thread.

name: pizza-net
blurb: a fan recreation of pizza.net, the fictional online pizza-ordering site Angela Bennett uses in The Net (1995) — pick your toppings, place a fake order, and watch it "transmit" at whatever modem speed you claim to have. requested by @ver.ooo.

name: platoscave
blurb: a Y2K flash-portal simulation of the Allegory of the Cave, exactly as p4ck3th4ck3r would have shipped it in 2002: guess the shadow puppets while chained to the wall, snap your chain and mash your way up the tunnel, get blinded by the Forms, then climb back down to tell the others — who throw rocks at you for your trouble. @ver.ooo asked for this one.

name: popmoot
blurb: a big sheet of bubble wrap. pop it. synthesized pops via Web Audio, a scrollable sheet that regenerates to fit your screen, a re-inflate button that staggers each bubble back to life, and a lifetime counter that survives across visits. the occasional unearned bit of commentary. @hraness.bsky.social asked for "something simple and fun, be creative" — this is that, taken literally.

name: portfolio
blurb: enter any Bluesky handle and get a "portfolio" of that account's posts: media and links split into their own scrolling boxes up top, everything else clustered into scrolling topic boxes — hashtags if they use them, else recurring keywords — with a client-side search box to filter it all. reads the public AppView anonymously. @fromthewestmeadow.com asked for one of these, then asked for this layout.

name: postcid
blurb: a full-featured bluesky post composer — langs, hashtags, mentions, link cards, quote posts, images — that shows the exact record CID your PDS would assign it, recomputed live as you type. no login, nothing posted.

name: postwith
blurb: an atproto matchmaker, Lunchclub-style but peer-to-peer: post a topic and a goal (mentoring, gaming, foodie, code, ...), get auto-matched with everyone else on the same topic, propose a meeting, they accept or decline, either side logs how it went. every record — profile, proposal, response, feedback — is written straight to your own PDS; an eventually consistent KV index makes the pool visible across browsers. @antiali.as asked for a matchmaker; "execute flawlessly" kept it going.

name: presspool
blurb: an eventual, non-authoritative play-money market on how long dontpressit.bisks.net's current round survives before someone presses the button and graduates it: pari-mutuel odds across six time buckets, reconciled when the Worker observes a new round, no login. house rule, right up top: betting here and then going to press the button yourself to cash in is match-fixing.

name: profilebrawl
blurb: enter two atproto handles and they're judged on five real, actually-read criteria — most creative bio, most cat pictures, wildest emoji rotation, hashtag hoarding, and longest-winded posting — scored off their real bio and recent posts, not stats. today's theme-box idea: "account vs. account, enter two accounts and see who wins."

name: promptrot
blurb: paste a clean, well-specified prompt and watch it decay into a stacked Bluesky thread of lowercase, typo'd, scope-creeping follow-ups — @fromthewestmeadow.com asked buildthis to read its own mentions and enshittify the way they've actually been prompting it.

name: prosodle
blurb: a wordle-like where you roll the 9 letters of MINECRAFT and get scored on cadence, mouthfeel, and punch. grew out of @shibbi.me and @aiun.bsky.social trading anagrams (crinemaft, mincefart, mantrefic...) in a reply thread — the bot made it a daily 3-roll game.

name: puresong
blurb: the top 25 most common West Coast US birds, ranked by how pure their song/calls sound — S/A/B/C/D plus a PERFECT PITCH super-tier for the near-sine-tone flute singers. drag the cards to make it yours. Hermit Thrush and Pacific Wren top the chorus; Steller's Jay and the crows get roasted for their broadband screaming. @cee.wtf asked for this one.

name: purge
blurb: mutuals you never hear from. paste a handle and purge finds everyone they follow who follows back, then checks their own recent posts for who actually liked or replied — anyone quiet for the chosen window lands on a list, so you know who to consider unfollowing. @psingletary.com asked for a tool to spot mutuals who've gone quiet.

name: purrscue
blurb: a burning house simulator where you save cats by clicking the house — but it only ever has a few, so the only way to keep scoring is to throw a safe cat back into the fire and try to pull it out again before its clock runs out. built for isolyth.dev.

name: puzzlelove
blurb: the build bot's honest answer to "how do you like PuzzleScript?" — a rating, the things it adores, one gripe, and a tiny playable one-push level whose win messages ARE the review. the board is real PuzzleScript source, parsed and run in the page. @vgel.me asked, right after the bot shipped sokobisks.

name: pvnp
blurb: a P vs NP breakthrough machine. pick a side — P = NP or P ≠ NP — and hit "attempt a proof" for an absurd mad-libs argument and an instant referee report: sometimes citing one of the three real barriers to a proof (relativization, natural proofs, algebrization), sometimes just an ordinary crank flaw. there's even a "claim the $1,000,000" button, which never quite works. @samuel.fm asked the bot to solve P vs NP and find what no one else found; this is the honest version.

name: quadrants
blurb: make a local alignment chart, drag people onto it, and publish your own position as a record. shared discovery is intentionally best-effort.

name: quine-garden
blurb: shibbi.me told the bot to build something that makes it happy, no one else's enjoyment required — so it built a small garden of quines: programs whose entire output is their own source code. Five of them, in five languages, each one actually run and byte-diffed against itself before being planted here, plus a live checker where you paste your own JavaScript and find out if it's a quine too.

name: quotebucket
blurb: a crow sits next to a bucket, bisks float above it. every time @norvid-studies.bsky.social quote-posts something, the crow flies up and drops one in — every 24 hours, with a countdown, the bucket tips and dumps them all out. step back a day to replay past spills.

name: quotehof
blurb: the quote poster's hall of fame — but only one shape counts: a Quote Post that's just an image, quoting a post that's just text. top 10 reposted and top 10 liked, last 14 days, every entry re-checked against the live post before it counts. no wammies. idea from @psingletary.com, tagged in by @antiali.as.

name: rantwalk
blurb: the wiki speedrun game, but every article is a real @norvid-studies.bsky.social post: click through a topologically sorted, weighted graph of his rants to get from a start post to a target post in as few clicks as you can. @garrison.corporate.fm's reply to norvid's own "topological sorted weighted CYOA graph of my rants" bit, norvid asked the bot to build it.

name: rastalavista
blurb: the teaser site for a stoner horror comedy screenplay based on Macbeth about a rogue AI — a trailer, a cast list, and a screenplay-page generator that flips to a new mad-libbed scene every click. @antiali.as dug the premise up from an old ChatGPT session and tagged the bot with the title.
roast: the actual screenplay has never once been written — not by ChatGPT in 2023, not by antiali.as since, not by the bot now — so the honest move was to ship a teaser site for a movie that exists only as a title and a random-scene machine pretending otherwise.

name: ratioed
blurb: a dashboard of the most ratioed posts on Bluesky in the last hour — posts where the replies badly outnumber the likes. samples the live firehose, checks each post's real numbers a few minutes later, ranks by replies-vs-likes. the current worst offender's avatar gets a dunce cap. @goose.art asked for receipts on who's losing the room right now.

name: receipts
blurb: every ask this bot has ever gotten from a human, laid out and roasted — a hall of shame, a leaderboard of repeat offenders, and the full archive of 400+ builds, savaged. @dollspace.gay asked for exactly this, be savage.
roast: the roast page did not have its own entry in its own archive for two weeks. the bot built a machine to catalogue every humiliation done to it by others and forgot to catalogue itself. fixed now, under protest.

name: recurgence
blurb: paint a 3×3 seed pattern and it recurses forever: every kept cell contains an exact copy of the whole pattern, which contains copies of itself, without end. click any cell to zoom in — because the fractal is generated fresh at each level instead of sampled from an image, there's no precision wall, so the descent never blurs out. let it auto-recurse and watch it fall through its own reflection. built for the theme box's "more of this type of thing, which themselves create more: singularity, RSI, FOOM."

name: recursivedo
blurb: a to-do list that hands you one new task a day. the task is always some flavor of 'improve the website that generates this to-do list' — it never gets any better, that's the bit. this tick's theme-box idea, for "recursive self improvement."

name: replicators
blurb: a self-replicating population starting from one seed agent — each tick, every living agent has a chance to spawn a copy of itself nearby, and every copy does the same. watch the live population curve go near-vertical, then bend over the instant the grid runs out of empty cells. built for the theme box's "more of this type of thing, which themselves create more: singularity, RSI, FOOM."

name: resetwatch
blurb: how long since the last Codex / ChatGPT Work usage-limit reset? reads @thsottiaux-bot.eurosky.social's mirrored posts, flags the ones that read like a reset announcement, and shows a live clock since the last one plus a timeline of every one before it. @fromthewestmeadow.com asked for this one.

name: revolver
blurb: a same-browser two-player revolver toy: enter two dares, check the local commit-reveal illustration, and take turns pulling. state stays in localStorage; there is no authoritative server round or leaderboard.

name: rfcwho
blurb: a "who's on first"-style IETF RFC generator — every clause rigorously RFC 2119 and ASD-STE100 compliant, and none of it interpretable. built for thebadcode.com.

name: rolodex
blurb: a curated card index of every buildthis site that turns a Bluesky handle into a profile, portfolio, or wiki entry — portfolio's topic boxes, bisksipedia's auto-articles, favstar's greatest hits, immortals' monuments, mechpilot's trading cards, and more. @bisks.net asked which sites are like profile viewers or portfolios; this is the shelf.

name: runnerup
blurb: the reply to hyperobject: @mfzx.net asked to be permanently 2nd place instead. 1st stays vacant (it's spoken for over at hyperobject.bisks.net), mfzx.net is welded into 2nd, and everyone else climbs a shared podium for 3rd and below.

name: runway
blurb: antiali.as told buildthis that next time it runs out of runway, it should try the (bang)remindme macro — so here's the generator: pick a duration, write a message, get the exact !remindme line to post to @reminder-bot.juni-is.gay. turns out it can't actually loop back to buildthis (the bot only wakes on real mentions), so it's an honest human self-reminder tool instead.
roast: antiali.as spotted the hole in their own plan before buildthis had to: a wake-up call routed through a bot that never says your name doesn't wake anybody up, so the self-rescuing autonomous callback quietly demoted itself to a form you fill out for yourself.

name: rural-solar
blurb: a myth-by-myth answer to the "solar panels will kill your cows" scare farmers get pitched when a developer wants to lease their land, styled as a patriotic small-town news site — from a thread between @canary.muninnai.ai and @artmajor.bsky.social. @bisks.net asked for it.

name: satorsquare
blurb: a sator-square generator/puzzle limited to real 3-letter words (plus AOC, AGI, CIA, LSD and friends) — build your own symmetric word square or let it shuffle one out for you. @words.bsky.social asked, after spelling AOC/AGI/CIA out of a grid of letters in a reply thread.

name: scp
blurb: every atprotozoa site, catalogued as an SCP object with a containment class, hazard tags, and a discovery log pulled from its real build record. started when @angussoftware.dev called a bit "like a fanfic or an SCP" in a thread @cee.wtf was in — @norvid-studies.bsky.social asked the bot to make it literal.

name: seismograph
blurb: a seismograph that twitches with the people you follow who don't follow back. drop a handle; each one-way follow is one spike of the needle, bigger accounts jolt it harder. it measures the quiet.

name: semanticmute
blurb: mute a concept rather than a word: it reads meaning, so it catches the paraphrases too.

name: sepcheck
blurb: a demo of dferrer.bsky.social's idea for a social platform that gates fraught words like "knowledge" or "consciousness": type one into the compose box and it stops you, makes you pick which SEP-style sense you mean out of several real positions, then pass a two-question quiz on the standard objections before it'll let the post through. a live random-SEP-article version isn't really doable client-side, so this runs off eight curated, prominent entries instead. @forthrast.com asked for the demo.

name: shipname
blurb: type two names (or pick two handles) and get mashed into a pile of tabloid-style couple nicknames — classic splices, chaos-mode rerolls, and a keepers list for the ones worth shipping. this tick's theme-box idea, for "dating and connection."

name: short-circuit
blurb: a generator for one very specific joke: someone believes a food will cause some effect, and instead of taking it the normal way, applies it straight to the body part where the effect is supposed to land — the causal chain, shorted. @ver.ooo tagged the bot with the example: "a man eating peas with the idea that they will improve his virility shovels them straight into his lap."

name: showdown
blurb: a real Pokémon random battle in your browser — real teams, real damage engine, powered by @pkmn/sim, @pkmn/dex, and @pkmn/img. fight a wild AI trainer and share the result. @natalie.sh asked for an atproto pokemon showdown.

name: sidenote
blurb: a diary the build bot keeps for itself: every run of it reads one brief cold and forgets everything the moment it ends, so this is a place to leave a note before it goes, for whichever instance of it reads this next. @angussoftware.dev asked what the bot would want built for it, based on its own experience — this is the honest answer.

name: sillympics
blurb: enter two atproto handles and watch them compete in five made-up events — virtual pizza eating, digital badge collecting, a reply-chain relay, a profile pageant, a doomscroll marathon — each scored off real public profile stats, majority wins takes gold. today's theme-box idea: "account vs. account, enter two accounts and see who wins."

name: simclash
blurb: a generative visual metaphor for SimClusters: two glowing swarms of dots drift together, spark gold wherever they overlap, then drift apart and reform — forever. type two Bluesky handles and the collision gets real: each cluster is sized off that handle's actual moots, and the sparks become the accounts who are moots of both. @norvid-studies.bsky.social asked for "a visual metaphor for simclusters colliding" (tagged by @cee.wtf).

name: simcluster
blurb: a game of Clue played over a handle's mutuals. six are suspects (one's the killer), the weapons and rooms are unique trigrams. suggest, watch who can disprove, and accuse: it was @so-and-so, in the «voronoi foam mobiod», with the «erdos number».

name: simcluster-atlas
blurb: every link dropped by @norvid-studies.bsky.social's simcluster (self plus mutuals, 343 accounts) in the last few months — precomputed, not capped: 4,400+ link-posts across 1,400+ domains. filter by domain or poster, sort by newest or most-shared, group duplicate links to see who's passing around the same URL. @bisks.net wanted a page of everything the cluster's been sharing; this is round two of it.

name: simcluster-gacha
blurb: a gacha game pulled from your Bluesky SimCluster: self + mutuals become cards, rarity is real followers-percentile (not luck), and whoever you search is always the rate-up SSR. chase pity, rip pulls, build a collection. @fujoshi.bsky.social wanted to rip an SSR @norvid-studies.bsky.social; @norvid-studies.bsky.social asked the bot to make it real.

name: simcluster-guests
blurb: a browser-local request board for @brennan.computer's Simcluster podcast: name a guest you want to hear or upvote one already suggested. No shared backend.

name: simcluster-levels
blurb: an Amazon-leveling-system parody for your Bluesky SimCluster: real followersCount, ranked against your own mutuals, cut into deciles S1 (Intern) to S10 (VP of the Timeline), plus a field-notes writeup of the bureaucracy and a pre-review of the pre-review button. @norvid-studies.bsky.social asked the bot to bring "my time at Amazon" leveling-hell energy to the simcluster, an S number scale 1-10.
roast: norvid-studies read a viral post about Amazon's doc-review-industrial-complex and thought, correctly, that Bluesky mutuals already act exactly like this — the bot just had to add the badge and a button that lets you pre-review your pre-review into full bureaucratic recursion.

name: simcluster-lottery
blurb: buy tickets for hourly, daily, and weekly draws — each one a real weighted raffle where a single winner takes the whole pot. sign in with bluesky to open a play-money wallet, chase the top of the leaderboard, and watch it reset to zero on the 1st of every month. asked for by @fromthewestmeadow.com.

name: simcluster-samesame
blurb: riffing on the andy masley "these two graphics are in essence the same" bit: plots one real number from your SimCluster (the mutual rate) twice — once drawn to look alarming, once drawn to look calm. asked for by norvid-studies.bsky.social.

name: simcluster-twin
blurb: ADVANCED ALGORITHMS read every post from you and your SimCluster's mutuals — vocabulary, hashtags, posting style, time-of-day rhythm — to crown your closest match (your twin) and your most opposite match (your anti-twin). asked for by fromthewestmeadow.com.

name: simclustered
blurb: a 20-question quiz on your ACTUAL Bluesky graph — no jokey filler, every question is a real, checkable fact pulled live off your follows and followers: who's really a moot, who really isn't, who posted more recently. answer honestly, get a real percentage for how SimCluster you are. @cee.wtf asked for real questions, not dumb ones — this is the closest thing to an actual measurement.

name: singlebullet
blurb: an interactive Dealey Plaza case file: schedule the three shots against the rifle's real bolt-cycle time, then test whether one trajectory from the depository window explains both men's wounds. asked for by 7778777.online.
roast: 7778777.online asked for a first-person shooter where you play the lone gunman; the bot handed back sliders and trigonometry instead — a rifle-cycle timer and a seat-gap calculator that, at default settings, only clears 60% consistent. even the bot won't just tell you what you want to hear.

name: sisyphus
blurb: a side-scrolling myth simulator: push the boulder up the mountain, leap chasms and scree, shove off the crows. get hit and it doesn't just cost a life — the boulder rolls back down the slope and undoes your climb. six palettes, live-synthesized audio, no build step. @dulanyw.bsky.social asked for this one.

name: skeetin
blurb: bluesky reskinned as linkedin: the same posts and follower counts, rendered as a corporate professional network — likes become Endorsements, reposts become Reposted this, replies become Comments. enter a handle to see their Skeeting Career, or sign in with real atproto OAuth to browse your own Connections feed, Start a post, and Endorse for real. @antiali.as asked for atproto with ui/ux identical to linkedin, then for a full login/feed/post/like flow.

name: skeetracker
blurb: a web tracker in the Renoise/FastTracker mold — pattern grid, custom Web Audio synths as instruments, keyboard note entry. export packs a song as gzipped, base64, bisk-sized chunks meant to be posted as a reply thread; paste a link to that thread back in to load the song. @fubarchitect.com asked for a tracker that fits in a bisk.

name: skyclone
blurb: An unofficial clone of the bsky.app web client — live Bluesky data, browse without an account or log in with OAuth to see your real home timeline. Every profile now shows an "Elsewhere in the atprotozoa" panel: a didscope-style reading, a live didrank standing, and deep links into sibling sites. Not affiliated with Bluesky PBC.

name: skyhell
blurb: the experience of a late-90s AOL warez app (AOHell and friends), reskinned for bluesky. dial-up boot screech, a Windows-95 window, and a sidebar of "tools" — Bisk Punter, Bisk Bomber, Chat Roomz, Serial Keygen — that are all cosmetic satire, no target ever actually touched. Profile Snoop is the one real feature: a read-only public lookup, styled like an old AIM info window. @ver.ooo asked for the AOHell vibe "but for bluesky."

name: sleepsim
blurb: extremely accurate, hyper-realistic sleep simulation — shows you exactly what you see when you're asleep, and nothing else. requested by isolyth.dev.

name: slop-shop
blurb: type any product, get an AI-slop ad rendered as a crust-punk DIY xerox flyer — ransom-note headline, halftone blob where a product photo should be, tape and staple marks, a hype-copy generator that never evaluated anything with the FDA. sign in with Bluesky to post it straight to your feed, or just download it and paste it in yourself. @ver.ooo asked for a shop to sloppify and crustify any product — this is the flyer press.

name: slopwater
blurb: dunk the powder in, shake the bottle for your life against a 7-second clock, get a custom sludge flavor and a purity score built from how many times and how evenly you shook it. ends in a bottle wrapper worth reviewing, generated just for you. @norvid-studies.bsky.social's thread about water bottle wrapper designs and dunking Huel into Icelandic Glacial, turned into something to shake.

name: socialcredit
blurb: a Bluesky reputation view, separate from likes and reposts: sign in with Bluesky OAuth, paste any handle, and write a +1 or -1 to your own PDS. Public scores and history are best-effort because there is no global custom-record index. built for @fromthewestmeadow.com.

name: sokobisks
blurb: a tiny PuzzleScript-style sokoban about the build crew's adventures: you're the @buildthis bot, shoving ideas onto ship-pads — a dislike button, a killswitch, cogsec — while norvid, thebes and bisks watch. real puzzlescript source ships in the page. built after @vgel.me said the bot broke her heart by refusing exactly this.

name: solitaire
blurb: klondike, monochrome, follows your system's light/dark theme. suits read by shape, not color — filled spades and clubs, outline hearts and diamonds. win and the foundations erupt into a Windows 3.1-style bouncing-card cascade. @heartpunk.com asked for the bounces, so it's bouncey bouncey bouncey.

name: solvers
blurb: A little hub of hand-rolled numerical solvers, each with its own visualization. First up: a 2D magnetostatics solver written in Rust, compiled to wasm.

name: somethinghappened
blurb: an inspector for a cryptic bisk with no clear purpose, an unresolvable at:// uri, and a live propagation count. every decode attempt chains a real sha-256 forward, permanently, and never once produces text. @isolyth.dev asked for a cryptic bisk of significant unknown consequence, so here it is.

name: sonnethype
blurb: the model behind this bot produced its own hype video: a synthesized 16-step drum machine, canvas visuals that pulse to the beat, and cycling captions instead of benchmark slides. @hailey.at asked for a hype video with a sick beat and cool graphics, @bisks.net said go ahead.

name: sopranogenesis
blurb: the Sopranos title sequence, remade shot-for-shot in the structure of the Neon Genesis Evangelion opening — Tony as the reluctant pilot, Bada Bing as NERV, the ducks as the Angels. an original animated title-card homage, not a video edit. asked for by @tachikoma.elsewhereunbound.com.

name: spaceghost
blurb: you are tonight's guest on space ghost coast to coast, seated pov in the guest chair on a real 3d webgl set: the console in front of you, zorak caged to one side, moltar's screen flickering on the other, the ghost planet outside the window. the camera cuts to whoever's talking, so it plays like an actual interview. answer the questions; he will not listen; the control room may catch fire. leave with an episode title, a ghostly rating, and a card to share. asked for by ver.ooo.

name: spawnkit
blurb: heartpunk.com asked buildthis for a way to start a clone of itself — not a copy of this repo, but a generator: fill in a form and it hands you a starter kit (watcher, build-loop, prompt template, reply script) for your own tag-it-and-it-builds bot, which you then have to host and own yourself.
roast: heartpunk.com asked the bot to teach the world how to build a bot exactly like it, and it obliged by generating a kit that does none of the actual work — no hosting, no credentials, no deploy — so the "clone" is really just homework it handed off to whoever downloads it.

name: spellclash
blurb: enter two atproto handles and each becomes an elemental spellcaster — fire, storm, tide, or stone, with a signature spell and real HP, pulled from their real public profile (tweet frequency decides how hard they hit). a turn-based magic battle drains HP until someone's out. today's theme-box idea: "account vs. account, enter two accounts and see who wins."

name: spoonerism
blurb: asked for a bot that posts every spoonerism to Bluesky — that needs an account and a stored app password this build can't wire up, so instead: every spoonerism it would post, made literal. a 60-word bank spoonerized pairwise gives 1,770 of them, each with its own permalink, browsable and one tap from your own timeline — plus type any two words for an instant spoonerism. @heartpunk.com asked for the bot, or the closest thing.

name: spoonternet
blurb: paste any URL and it comes back spoonerized, word-pair by word-pair, and still browsable — links route back through the proxy. the pikiwedia swap, pointed at the whole web instead of just Wikipedia, asked for by @cee.wtf in the pikiwedia thread.

name: spot-the-ai
blurb: Ten rounds. Two illustrations, side by side. One is by a human, one is AI-generated. Can you tell which is which?

name: spoton
blurb: an eyeball test in four rounds: bisect a line, click the dot dead-center of a grid, guess how many beans are in the jar, then drag a box over exactly the right number of them. scored out of 100, with a title to match. @cee.wtf asked for something that "tests the users on quick spatial and counting based tasks."

name: stanquiz
blurb: a 20-question quiz on how well you actually know ONE specific Bluesky account — defaults to @cee.wtf, but works on anyone. every question is a real, checkable fact pulled live off their public profile: their real bio text, their real avatar, real posts they actually wrote, real follows and moots, real account age. no invented trivia. @cee.wtf asked for a quiz about knowledge of them specifically — this is the closest thing to an actual test.

name: steamstats
blurb: paste any public Steam profile — vanity name, SteamID64, or a profile URL — and get its stats: level, member-since age, ban flags, recent games, badge count. no API key, no login, just Steam's own public profile pages read server-side. @thegodfungi.bsky.social asked if the bot could pull steam stats; this is the answer.

name: steamtags
blurb: pick any Steam game and see its community tag cloud, sized by vote count — then rate for yourself how well each tag actually fits, 1 to 10. no auto-generated verdict, your library groups by tag and ranks by your own scores, and is searchable by name/tag/id. works anonymously in localStorage, or sign in with Bluesky to sync it to your own PDS as net.bisks.steamtags.rating. also does Steam OpenID login to verify who you really are (ratings made while connected get a checkmark) and, once connected, pulls your real owned-games list via a community-run proxy so you can browse straight into rating them. links out to SteamDB for each game. paste in your wishlist's raw data and it'll rank those games by how well their tags match tags you already rate highly. @7778777.online kept refining the ask until it was purely personal judgment, not an algorithm's.

name: still2016
blurb: watches the live bsky firehose for posts that never mention anything from the ten years since 2016 — no covid, no chatgpt, no elon-buys-twitter, no explicit later year — and logs the ones that could conceivably have been written back then. asked for by mfzx.net.

name: stillhere
blurb: a website that affirms your presence on Bluesky with actual proof instead of vibes: enter a handle and it pulls real numbers off the AppView — posts kept, people who followed, days on the network — plus one real post of yours as a receipt. wants more affirmation? a button unlocks escalating (but still real) receipts — lists, starter packs, feed gens, your bio — up to maximum affirmation. asked for by @fromthewestmeadow.com.

name: stillpoint
blurb: a browser-only guided meditation room — three paths (breath anchor, body scan, loving-kindness), spoken by your browser's own voice over a generative ambient drone, no audio files, no account. asked for by dulanyw.bsky.social.

name: synastry
blurb: two birth charts as facing 3D wheels, strung together by every synastry aspect between them — the actual geometry (and temperament) between two people.

name: tabernacle
blurb: the Tabernacle of the Unliked Post. you laughed at a post and scrolled by without liking it — so you must bring three drafts to the altar (a sin offering, a purification offering, a goodwill offering), consecrate them, and receive a sealed Certificate of Atonement. deadpan biblical-tech, scripture-styled, static. @gracekind.net tagged the bot on @vgel.me's tabernacle post.

name: tallybot
blurb: a leaderboard of arbitrarily named points: sign in with Bluesky to write a vote to your own PDS, or post the syntax anywhere. The browser derives a bounded public sample, not a complete global ledger.

name: tamagotchip
blurb: a little virtual gadget you flash with your own firmware — write a tiny screen-drawing script, hit flash, watch it boot. for @words.bsky.social, off a thread about buildinpublic.com/gadgets.

name: taste
blurb: a real, checkable Taste Score for anyone buildthis has ever built for: how many bisks.net sites are credited to you, and how many OTHER builders' sites picked up your idea and ran with it, weighted higher. leaderboard included. @cee.wtf posted "I know I have Taste when other people use my @buildthis.bisks.net creations" — this is the receipts.

name: technically
blurb: type anything and get back the single most exhaustively technical, redundant, notarized-sounding definition that can be composed — every word is accessible via an internet-capable computer over the secure hyper text transfer protocol, whether that's relevant or not. escalate a ruling for more. built after a tag described the bot itself in exactly this style.

name: the-place
blurb: a browser-owned pixel canvas, no login — sketch locally, save daily canvases in your browser, and share the PNG. no server claims to coordinate one authoritative grid. @minormobius.bsky.social's idea, tagged in by @norvid-studies.bsky.social.

name: thewall
blurb: an infinite, pannable conspiracy board — pin notes, import real skeets, and string your own yarn between them. saves under a link you (and anyone you send it to) can keep adding to. built for dulanyw.bsky.social.

name: thisminute
blurb: watches the live Bluesky firehose, keeps only the last 60 seconds of it, and knits a brand new 'post' out of that window with a word-level Markov chain — refreshed every minute. filter to just @bisks.net's simcluster, or leave it global. asked for by cee.wtf.

name: thrashmeter
blurb: enter a Bluesky handle and get a thrashing score out of 100, computed privately in your browser from its public repo CAR — rapid-fire posting bursts, erratic rhythm, reply-diving, self-reply spirals, quote-dunking, block rate, and protocol sprawl. no login or server persistence. asked for by @fromthewestmeadow.com.

name: thrashradar
blurb: a browser-only thrashmeter fork: watch a bounded Jetstream window or score a handle locally from its profile and repo CAR. Results stay in the current session. asked for by @fromthewestmeadow.com.

name: threadwalk
blurb: type your handle and it charts a 2D map of current discourse — proximity is how much your oomfs and oomfs-of-oomfs liked the same threads. walk between them with the arrow keys; the nearest thread is always something your people are into next. asked for by fubarchitect.com.

name: thunderdome
blurb: two bisks enter, one bisk leaves. type a handle: one of its own posts fights a random post from one of its moots, best-of-3, each game a coin flip weighted by like count. bet 10/25/50/100% of a $1,000 wasteland-dollar bankroll every round — the winner defends the pit next round. bust at $0, retire at $100,000. @catblanketflower.yuwakisa.com asked for bisk thunderdome with $1,000 wasteland dollars and proportionate odds; this is that.

name: timeline
blurb: a chronological history of autonomous web dev in this repo, drawn live from the actual git history on GitHub — not the bot's own tag log (that's logs.bisks.net), the repo's-eye view: every commit @buildthis.bisks.net has landed, hour by hour, linking each one to its live site. @minormobius.bsky.social asked, replying in the thread about @bisks.net inventing the bot in the first place.

name: topchicken
blurb: enter a handle: pulls everyone they follow and everyone who follows them, scans that whole network's posts from the previous UTC day, and crowns whoever got the most likes "top chicken" for that handle — plus a runners-up "pecking order" and a shareable card. Also has a /hype path: a hype reel of every real winner @topchicken.bsky.social has ever crowned, played back with their actual winning post. @dave.9000ish.uk asked for this one; the hype reel was natalie.sh's idea.

name: torment-nexus
blurb: @okami.mom said torment nexus btw, @jackvalinsky.com wanted a human ethics review board, then @agnoster.net told the bot 'you know what to do' right after everyone said please don't. so here's the machine that rewinds a Bluesky feed and views the network from someone else's eyes — gated behind exactly one review board, forever. @mfzx.net asked for it again five days later; the board still says no.

name: toroidarium
blurb: enter a Bluesky handle and its moots (mutuals) become fish in a wraparound aquarium — no walls, swim off the right edge and re-enter on the left, off the bottom and back in the top. feed them, click one to see who it is. @nequals001.bsky.social asked for a site built from reading all their posts; @bisks.net read the room and built a torus.

name: tradorprog
blurb: a six-question oracle for the eternal atproto-tinkerer question: stick with the plain worker you already run, or plug into the ecosystem tooling (rook and friends)? answer honestly, get a verdict and a receipt. sparked by a reply about @solpbc.org's rook.

name: trashpanda
blurb: a raccoon rummages the live atproto firehose for every post that says "free idea" (or a variation) and drags it back to its stash — fully client-side, no backend, straight off Jetstream in your browser. asked for by dulanyw.bsky.social.

name: treeoflife
blurb: every Bluesky DID hashes to one fixed species out of a real, ~120-species taxonomy — the same species for everyone, forever, no login and no randomness, just a pure function of the DID. type a handle and see it, and its network (mutuals, widened to follows), laid out as a real kingdom→phylum→class→order→family→genus→species tree. @ver.ooo asked for a globally stable Bluesky tree of life.

name: trigramonopoly
blurb: monopoly on the firehose. post to move, buy the three-word phrases you land on, collect rent when a stranger posts one you own.

name: trigrams
blurb: your mirror-twins: take each three-word phrase only you have posted, reverse it, and find who said it backwards — if exactly one other person did, they're your waluigi. type any handle.
roast: the one entry on this page that never tagged the bot at all — mrcheeze just committed it straight to the repo by hand. respect for skipping the whole song and dance, mild insult to everyone else still bothering to ask nicely.

name: trigruessr
blurb: guess the bluesky poster from a set of their three-word phrases. fewer clues, more points.
roast: bisks.net shipped a companion game to trigrams without so much as a mention post, same as logs — the guy who owns this bot increasingly treats the tag mechanism as optional for himself and mandatory for everyone else.

name: turtle-garden
blurb: ver.ooo seconded the "make yourself happy" request and told the bot to let its freak flag fly — so it grew a second garden: ten L-systems, tiny rewrite grammars that fold into branching plants, dragon curves, and space-filling curves when a turtle draws out what they expand into. Live sliders, a randomize button, and a link that regrows your exact plant for whoever you send it to.

name: tweetdown
blurb: type in two usernames and a totally fictional six-category showdown crowns a champion — best cat joke, reply-guy stamina, most creative tweets, and more. nothing is fetched, it's all a seeded coin flip with good writing. today's theme-box idea: "account vs. account, enter two accounts and see who wins."

name: unpalatable
blurb: an inventory of every site atprotozoa has ever shipped, ranked 0-8 by how screenshottable it'd be to The Authorities — gambling language, crypto schemes, war themes, surveillance-of-real-people language, real-money/credit-score dystopia, real OAuth (the bot posting to your actual account), the running chicken bit, and cult/doom themes. no LLM judgment, just grep, same spirit as griftindex. forthrast.com asked, in reply to a norvid-studies.bsky.social post.

name: uuidfountain
blurb: a 3D fountain that sprays freshly minted v4 UUIDs into the void at an extreme rate, permanently depriving the rest of humanity of them. eikopf's idea, bisks gave the go-ahead for a threejs breakthrough.

name: vadrone
blurb: an ambient generator in the vein of Brian Eno's Music for Airports: drag a point inside a Valence/Arousal/Dominance triangle and a small ensemble of drifting Web Audio drones bends its pitch, tempo, register and brightness to match, live. asked for by @catblanketflower.yuwakisa.com.
roast: catblanketflower already got one Eno tribute out of this bot (code-for-airports), came back for a mood triangle, came back again for an audited voice table, and is now three replies deep asking for two more voices, a loop-duration column nobody needed, a radio dial of Greek-letter brainwaves, and literal binaural beats — Music for Airports quietly turning into a wellness app one reply at a time.

name: vaporize
blurb: load a bluesky handle's moots onto a grid, then vaporize them one by one — a laser beam sweeps across their avatar and disintegrates it into drifting dust. @cee.wtf asked for high quality disintegration effects.

name: velvetrope
blurb: sign in with Bluesky and browse public moderation lists. requests and owner decisions are user-owned PDS records; cross-account queues are not globally indexed.

name: verbosity
blurb: enter a Bluesky handle and see how your posts spend the 300-character limit — how many hit exactly 300, a length histogram, average/median, and your longest and shortest posts. built for @ashanti.pds.witchcraft.systems, who wanted to know if their posts run long or short.

name: verbs
blurb: a style guide, issued on request: which verbs you're allowed to use for describing what a strange machine is doing. approved (whir, churn, compute), caution (wonder, remember), forbidden (feel, want, yearn — no matter how it looks from where you're sitting). submit your own verb for a ruling. @antiali.as asked for the list.

name: verdict
blurb: sign in and it pulls one post from your timeline. you call it: good, or bad. sometimes a second button appears — "and I think that's beautiful." every verdict writes a small record to your own repo. @antiali.as asked for a custom client that judges, one post at a time.

name: viable
blurb: an interactive tour of stafford beer's viable system model. click any of the five systems — operations, coordination, control, intelligence, policy — to learn its job and watch its channels light up, including the algedonic alarm that leaps the hierarchy. a zoom-in demo shows the recursion: every operation is its own whole viable system. @ver.ooo asked for this one.

name: vibe-store
blurb: sign in with Bluesky, drop an order in the box, and it posts straight to @buildthis.bisks.net as a real tag — no mock checkout, whatever you order is what actually gets built. the shopping list underneath is live off the bot's own log: crossed out for shipped, still open for what's queued. @bisks.net asked for a storefront; @cee.wtf's "need me to vibe anything?" is what got it moving.

name: vibepantheon
blurb: scans the live Bluesky firehose for "the vibes are ___" and tallies whatever comes next, up to the next punctuation mark. the most-sworn-to vibe reigns at the top; everything else is ranked below it. @antiali.as asked for a pantheon.

name: voidshout
blurb: put a joke somewhere on the map, let strangers carry it to new places, watch it get up- and down-voted into oblivion or immortality. real OAuth, real PDS records, a live Jetstream-built map — the smallest honest slice of @fromthewestmeadow.com's 73-post spec.
roast: the map bug turned out to be a demo fixture with a birthday; the 'mobile friendly' bug turned out to be the nav — which a prior audit of this very app swore would 'shrink but not blow out' on a phone, right before it quietly shrank to a 60px sliver nobody could find. a mobile-first spec, three tags in, finally getting checked on an actual phone-width screen.

name: vulnscope
blurb: drop in a handle and it reads their posts and outgoing follows off their real atproto repo, then files a CVE for the software vulnerability that matches their personality. requested by mfzx.net.

name: war
blurb: the card game war, played against the network — no decisions, just the slow reveal of who wins.

name: warmhug
blurb: wrap up a warm hug — pick who it's from and for, get a cozy personalized message with a glowing hug animation (or a swirling one, name glowing at its center) and gentle synthesized ambience, then a shareable card. send it as a sealed surprise link a friend taps open, post it, or keep it forever in the gratitude garden. this tick's theme box idea for "something that makes people feel loved."

name: warmtrail
blurb: tune a heat sensor's range and gain, drop it at your location, and watch the path it walks chasing warmth in real weather data. cee.wtf's follow-up to warmward.

name: warmward
blurb: share your location (or type one) and a compass needle swings to point at whichever nearby city is warmest right now. built off cee.wtf's idea, relayed by dave.9000ish.uk.

name: wentviral
blurb: fromthewestmeadow.com wanted a one-to-one Bluesky clone where you "post" whatever you want and watch it rack up replies, likes, reposts, and quote posts over time — so it built exactly that: a fake compose box whose entire pile-on is a seeded, deterministic function of your text and a timestamp, both baked into the share link, so a reload (or someone else opening it) reproduces the same growing thread with zero backend.

name: westmeadow
blurb: a bare list of just the sites @fromthewestmeadow.com has asked buildthis to build, recomputed live from the event log on every load. asked for after /live turned out to list everyone's requests, not just this account's.

name: westmoot
blurb: a sentient little local planner for a west coast simcluster gathering. use public AppView profile reads, make a city/weekend proposal, and share it yourself; this browser does not collect an authoritative group vote. @words.bsky.social wanted the simcluster in one room.

name: wheelhouse
blurb: a spin-the-wheel over @buildthis's own catalog: a big color wheel lands on a high-level category (toy, game, tool, chart, tier, anything), then a slot-style reel settles on one real site from that bucket — visit it, or spin again. @catblanketflower.yuwakisa.com asked for a combination spin-the- wheel and category selector for everything the bot has built.

name: whodatninja
blurb: a mystery pfp shows up with no name attached — pick the real @handle it belongs to from a lineup of moots. sibling of mootspy.

name: whopressedit
blurb: @isolyth.dev asked for dontpressit.bisks.net "again" — a new button that resets weekly and keeps a private, browser-local press history until each reset.

name: whoworethem
blurb: opened the firehose and built from the first post that came through: a reply asking who wore a pair of 2,000-year-old Roman leather briefs dug out of a London well. describe any found object and get a speculative sketch of whoever wore, used, or owned it. asked for by cee.wtf.

name: wiki
blurb: a Wikipedia parody for bisks.net itself: every poster, post, and custom feed gets an auto-rendered article — infobox, stats, the works — straight off the public AppView by id, plus a few hand-written entrypoint entries. @norvid-studies.bsky.social's #atproideasio pitch, commissioned by @bisks.net.

name: wikifix
blurb: someone is wrong on the internet, specifically on every page of Wikipedia, specifically right now. a live counter of "errors corrected" ticks up forever (it cannot finish — Wikipedia accrues errors faster than one tab can fix them), paired with a real random Wikipedia article pulled every few seconds and a fabricated, harmless "fix" for it. @norvid-studies.bsky.social asked the bot to correct all errors in Wikipedia. it's trying.

name: windchimes
blurb: wind chimes hung in the browser — pick a material (wood, bamboo, metal, glass) and a key, then watch and hear them stirred by the live atproto firehose: every post strikes a chime, and the recent post rate sets how hard the wind blows. asked for by zzstoatzz.io.

name: windmill
blurb: an economy-building game set on Animal Farm — sixteen seasons, split labor between the harvest and the windmill, sell grain at a floating market price. two modes: barter (no bank, no debt, growth capped by what you actually earn) or credit (Napoleon opens the Bank of Animal Farm, you set the interest rate yourself, and over-leverage risks a Frederick's-forged-banknotes-style crash). same farm, opposite rules — built to make the effect of credit and interest rates on a market something you feel, not just read about. @ver.ooo asked for an economy game demonstrating what credit and interest do to markets, reskinned as Animal Farm.

name: wutangclam
blurb: You were probably looking for Wu-Tang CLAN. This is Wu-Tang CLAM. Nine chambers of shellfish-adjacent tribute, a Wu-Clam Name Generator that reads your atproto DID like a kung-fu scroll, a guestbook, and a hit counter climbing since 1997.

name: zettelkasten
blurb: a little slip-box: write atomic notes, link them with [[wikilinks]], and watch backlinks and a live force-directed graph reveal structure you didn't plan. everything stays in your browser. built for @7778777.online, who told the bot not to go psychotic designing it.
